scope: Validate DB migrations are reversible (down() implementation present + safe)
method: Step 1: grep down() presence on last 10 2026_05 migrations
Step 2: read each migration source for destructive/dangerous patterns
Step 3: php artisan migrate:rollback --pretend --step=10 --env=testing (NO real changes)
Step 5: php artisan migrate:status (count applied vs pending)
Step 6: cross-check ordering for timestamp collisions

environment.notes: Only --pretend / migrate:status used. Zero rows mutated. No migrate:fresh. Compliant with mission CAUTION.

migrations_examined.purpose: SQLite parity triggers for z_reports/order_payments NF525 DELETE-immutability
migrations_examined.notes: down() throws RuntimeException in prod (NF525 immutability locked). Non-prod drops triggers. SQLite-only up().
Same pattern: production rollback refused, non-prod drops triggers. MySQL+SQLite parity.

migrations_examined.purpose: Add user_id to orders idempotency UNIQUE (cross-customer leak fix)
migrations_examined.notes: Non-prod down() restores OLD UNIQUE before dropping NEW (no constraint gap window). Production refuses (NF525-adjacent).

migrations_examined.purpose: One-shot clear of fake-seeded allergen data
migrations_examined.notes: down() is intentional NOOP — refuses to re-introduce fake data. Documented in docblock. Skips closed orders (NF525 immutability preserved). Idempotent on replay.

migrations_examined.purpose: Composite UNIQUE on (branch_id, machine_id) for kiosk_machines
migrations_examined.notes: No prod guard — non-NF525 table. dropUnique try/catch idempotent.
Production refuses. Non-prod restores INDEX before dropping UNIQUE (no FK index gap).

migrations_examined.purpose: Add nullable pos_session_id column for cashier audit
migrations_examined.notes: down() drops column + index. ANY pos_session_id values populated by POS cashier path will be lost. Acceptable: audit-only column, not NF525-immutable. No prod guard but column is nullable + audit-grade.

migrations_examined.purpose: New table for QR signed-nonce replay protection
migrations_examined.notes: down() = Schema::dropIfExists(). Consumed nonces destroyed on rollback would re-open replay window. 6-month retention so impact is bounded.

migrations_examined.purpose: stock_movements DELETE/UPDATE triggers + FK cascadeOnDelete -> restrictOnDelete
migrations_examined.notes: down() drops triggers + restores cascadeOnDelete FKs. No prod-throw guard but docblock states 'Production should normally NEVER rollback.' Mild gap: silent rollback in production is possible. RECOMMENDATION: align with NF525 pattern (add app()->environment('production') throw).

migrations_examined.purpose: SQLite parity triggers for delivery_boy cash DELETE-immutability
migrations_examined.notes: down() drops SQLite triggers. MySQL prod is no-op (deploy doc handles). Safe by design.

rollback_pretend_output.notes: All 10 migrations produced valid rollback SQL with no exceptions. Step ordering preserves FK constraints (UNIQUE added before INDEX dropped, INDEX restored before UNIQUE dropped on down).

migrate_pretend_output.notes: All migrations applied; schema is at HEAD.

timestamp_collisions.rationale: Disjoint tables (webhook_events vs delivery_boy_cash_sessions). Filename alphabetic order resolves Laravel sort deterministically. Both apply cleanly on fresh DB.

findings.title: All 10 recent migrations have down() implementations
findings.detail: 10/10 down() blocks present. 7/10 use 'app()->environment("production") throw' guard for NF525-adjacency. 1/10 is intentional NOOP (Wave Q-4 fake allergen clear).

findings.title: stock_movements migration lacks prod-throw guard
findings.detail: 2026_05_18_140000_add_stock_movements_immutability_triggers.php docblock says 'Production should normally NEVER rollback' but down() does not enforce it via throw — silent rollback in prod is possible if invoked. Consistency gap vs other NF525-adjacent migrations. RECOMMENDATION: add the same throw pattern.

findings.title: Timestamp collision at 2026_05_18_120000 is safe
findings.detail: Two migrations share timestamp (webhook_events FK + delivery_boy_cash_sessions creation). They touch disjoint tables and alphabetical filename order resolves Laravel sort deterministically. No risk.

findings.title: loyalty_qr_nonces_consumed + pos_session_id columns destroy data on down()
findings.detail: Data-loss on rollback is acceptable: audit-only column / replay-protection table, not NF525-immutable fiscal evidence. Recovery requires re-population which is anti-replay safe.

verdict_summary: All 10 recent migrations have working, dry-run-validated down() implementations. NF525-adjacent migrations correctly refuse production rollback via RuntimeException. Non-NF525 migrations are fully reversible. One INFO-level consistency observation (MIG-OBS-2: stock_movements migration could add production-guard for pattern consistency).
